where: Section 1, sentence 'Only the kernel is common to every distro'
problem: This contradicts the list given just above it, which presents the shell, core utilities and package manager as parts of every distribution. A student can read the two statements as opposites, and in practice almost every distro also carries a shell and some core utilities (not always Bash).
fix: The one component every distro is built around is the Linux kernel; the shell, tools, package manager and desktop vary from distro to distro (Alpine, for example, ships a different shell and C library).

problem: 'Ubuntu and Fedora run the same Linux kernel' can be read as saying the kernel binary is identical. The two distros usually ship different kernel versions with different patches.
fix: Ubuntu and Fedora both use the Linux kernel, often at different versions, but differ in installer, package manager and default tools.

problem: The question does not separate dual boot from a virtual machine: dual boot also keeps all Windows files (it only shrinks a partition). A student can defend either answer, so the question has no single correct option as worded.
fix: Ask which option keeps Windows files and needs no change to the existing Windows disk or partitions. Answer: virtual machine, because it stores Linux in a disk image file and never repartitions; dual boot also keeps the files but requires shrinking a partition to make room.
